seo.title: Email
seo.seo_description: A system sorts your email, summarizes each request and drafts a reply from your own documents. Nothing is sent without your team's approval. See how it works.

translation.headline: Sorted email. Replies ready to review.
translation.subheadline: A system reads incoming email, classifies it, drafts a reply from your documents and waits for your go-ahead before sending anything.

blocks.role: Le problème, avec un exemple précis.

translation.title: The problem, day to day.
translation.body:
Take a renovation company. Every day brings price requests, questions about a job's progress, supplier invoices and unrelated messages. Someone opens everything, sorts, digs for the history, writes. The urgent message waits behind three others.

The example is constructed to illustrate the principle; it is not a customer's result.

items.title: Sorting.
items.text: Telling a price request from an invoice, and the urgent from what can wait.

items.title: Searching.
items.text: Finding the latest quote, the clause, the file number.

items.title: Writing.
items.text: Replying politely and completely, in the house style.

blocks.role: Ce que fait le système : quatre étapes, la dernière attend une personne.

translation.title: What the system does.
translation.intro: The workflow reacts when an email arrives in the mailbox we have connected to WorkStudio. Every step is visible and editable.

cards.title: It notices.
cards.text: A new email triggers the workflow. Only the mailboxes you choose to connect are read.

cards.title: It classifies.
cards.text: Category (price request, invoice, complaint, other), urgency and a one-sentence summary.

cards.title: It drafts.
cards.text: A reply draft, written to your style instructions and from your documents.

cards.title: It waits.
cards.text: A person reviews, edits, approves or refuses. Nothing goes out before.

translation.title: What your team receives.
translation.body: The team no longer works in the disorder of an inbox: it receives items ready to review.

items.title: A sorted queue.
items.text: Messages arrive classified by category and urgency.

items.title: A summary per message.
items.text: One sentence to understand without reading it all.

items.title: A draft per reply.
items.text: To correct, not to write. The style comes from instructions you version: the one in production and the one being tested stay separate.

items.title: A trace of every draft.
items.text: Which model, which request, which reply: everything can be consulted.

translation.title: The expected benefit.
translation.body: Less manual sorting, urgent items seen sooner, more consistent replies from one person to the next. We announce no percentage and no time saved: they depend on your volume and your rules, and are measured during a pilot, on your own email.

cards.title: Nothing goes out without a go-ahead.
cards.text: A person's approval comes before any sending, unless you decide otherwise in writing.

cards.title: You write the sorting rules.
cards.text: The categories, the urgency thresholds and the cases never to handle automatically are yours.

cards.title: You choose the mailboxes.
cards.text: Each connection belongs to a workspace and can be removed.

cards.title: The model is a written choice.
cards.text: On your server or in our infrastructure; an external model only with your agreement, and its location is shown.

cards.title: No bulk sending.
cards.text: This solution replies to requests received. It is not meant for sending promotional email.

blocks.role: FAQ propre à la solution courriels.

items.question: Does it work with my mail service?
items.answer: That depends on the service. A broad catalogue of services connects to WorkStudio, but each mail service is qualified during the diagnosis, and some connections require an administrator to register an application with the provider first.

items.question: Can the AI get a reply wrong?
items.answer: Yes, like a hurried person. That is why a human approves every send, why every draft leaves a trace and why a safeguard can check that the reply stays faithful to your documents before it reaches you. The safeguard reduces error; it does not make it impossible.

items.question: Can it answer simple cases on its own?
items.answer: Technically yes. In our setups, human approval is the rule; removing that step for one specific type of message is a decision you make in writing, which we record.

items.question: How long to put it into service?
items.answer: There is no universal timeline: it depends on your mail service, your rules and your documents. It is measured on a first case.

translation.title: See your email sorted.
translation.text: We prepare a demonstration on fictional email, then we talk about your mail service and your rules.
